The first and third acts of this movie are great, but I can't deny the fact that I did find the second act to be a bit of a drag, even though it still did have its moments. I still think it's a pretty solid western overall, mainly due to how cool the characters are, but I'm definitely not on the train of people that consider these films to be amazing thus far. But who knows, maybe I'll feel differently about The Good, the Bad, and the Ugly. I really hope so at least.

I imagine Colonel Mortimer bending down to pick up his hat only for it to be shot away at the last second over and over is the Wild West equivalent of you reaching for the car door only for your friend to drive forward a few metres over and over.

five minutes into this, clint eastwood is introduced in silhouette, riding into town in the dead of night in a storm. ennio morricone is pulling out his best whistler for the job. like it’s insane. i’m googling man with no name poncho immediately. and then it cuts to a close-up shot of eastwood, head bowed, hat brim covering his eyes, lighting a cigarillo and raising his head JUST AS A PEAL OF THUNDER HITS. i’m leant all the way forward. i’m moaning. i’m yowling. i’m going insane. it’s plainly the coolest thing i’ve ever seen. the next 2 hours is just cool scenes upon cool scenes (van cleef’s massive stupid revolver! “you have until the music stops to try”! eastwood’s little wave as he lights a stick of dynamite! “very careless of you old man - try this. now we start”!) that is ALMOST as cool as this minute of film. like it’s mad. he’s probably the coolest character ever created probably. he’s a fucking cowboy with a big gun and endless little cigars and a flare for the dramatic and a CAPE and he’s FUNNY he’s a CHEEKY little bugger he’s got a DASHING little vest i am obsessed with him good lord

WHAT A BADASS DUO ! It’s was a great sequel to the first one. You can already see Leone refining his style, both in the originality of his shots and in the musical score. The script doesn’t repeat itself. It’s different while maintaining the exact same tone, and also adding more emotional depth to the whole thing. Both characters have an unmatched aura. They feel equally powerful, but in reality, they are very different from each other and complement one another perfectly. The only thing I didn’t like, and something I generally dislike in movies, is when the same actor plays different characters in different parts of a franchise, especially when one of those characters is the main villain.
I enjoyed the small town rivalry plot of the first one more, but loved the colonel and camera work of this one. Both really good and excited for the final installment of this trilogy.

Unlike most people, I think the first movie is better. I believe the first movie's linear, protagonist-focused structure is superior to the second one's disjointed structure. However, in terms of action and cinematography, this movie has the edge over the first.

Clint Eastwood Signature Collection #2 Deuxième opus de la trilogie des Dollars et on s'approche de ce qui se fera de mieux dans le western italien avec le trio Eastwood / Van Cleef / Volonte mais aussi toutes les "gueules" du genre ( Luigi Pistili , Mario Brega , Aldo Sambrell etc...) et en bonus le jeune Klaus Kinski qui montre qu'il n'a pas besoin de beaucoup de texte ou de temps d'écran pour marquer le spectateur. La musique fait partie intégrante du film et accompagne parfaitement l'action et les personnages.

Uma direção excelente, com uma construção de tensão impecável acompanhada por uma trilha sonora marcante que define perfeitamente a atmosfera de faroeste. A dupla de protagonistas funciona muito bem, com personalidades diferentes, mas complementares. O ritmo é lento e pode parecer repetitivo, mas aproveita esse tempo para desenvolver o mistério e preparar os confrontos finais. A revelação dá ainda mais peso à história, e o desfecho é muito satisfatório, com ambos os protagonistas alcançando exatamente o que buscavam: a vingança e o dinheiro.

Je rattrape mes classiques ! Après avoir vu Pour une poignée de dollars que je n'avais pas trop adoré, lui préférant d'ailleurs largement Yojimbo de Kurosawa, je viens de finir Et pour quelques dollars de plus, le deuxième de la trilogie, avant d'aller découvrir Le Bon, la Brute et le Truand au cinéma en 4K ce soir. Contrairement au premier volet un peu plus artisanal, ce film est beaucoup plus froid, méthodique et perfectionné. L'histoire suit deux chasseurs de primes rivaux aux méthodes opposées qui se retrouvent sur la même piste : celle de l'Indien, chef de gang psychopathe évadé qui prépare le braquage de la banque d'El Paso. D'un côté, on a Monco (Clint Eastwood) qui chasse pour l'appât du gain pur et dur, et de l'autre le colonel Douglas Mortimer (Lee Van Cleef), guidé par une vengeance personnelle et intime. Le cœur du film repose sur cette cupidité. Sergio Leone oppose le matérialisme décomplexé de l'Amérique naissante avec Clint qui compte chaque cadavre en dollars au code d'honneur chevaleresque et tragique de Mortimer, pour qui l'argent ne vaut rien face au sang versé. Côté acting, c'est du lourd. Clint Eastwood affine son mythe en pure économie de mouvements, mâchoire serrée sur son cigare, regard plissé sous le chapeau : du vrai aura farming qui fait le contrepoids parfait au reste du casting. Lee Van Cleef a un profil d'aigle, un port altier et un regard d'acier teinté de mélancolie et d'aristocratie, avec une autorité naturelle qui lui permet presque de voler la vedette. Gian Maria Volontè livre une performance fiévreuse, constamment sous l'emprise de la fumette avec ses rires sardoniques et ses folies meurtrières. Mention spéciale à la surprise de voir Klaus Kinski dans le rôle du bossu Wild ! Visuellement, Leone maîtrise ses très grands angles panoramiques dans le désert d'Almería, avec des coupes brutales vers des gros plans assez extrêmes sur les yeux, les fronts moites et les mains gantées. La musique d'Ennio Morricone vit à l'intérieur de l'histoire, complètement diégétique via la boîte à musique de la montre à gousset, véritable symbole du temps, de la mémoire et du trauma : quand la mélodie s'arrête, on sait que ça sent mauvais. Le climax final est un pur opéra, la caméra tournant autour des tireurs en suivant les montées chromatiques des trompettes et des cloches. Un très bon film, j'espère que Le Bon, la Brute et le Truand sera à la hauteur de celui-là.

"Where life had no value, death, sometimes, had its price. That is why the bounty killers appeared." Even though it is widely considered and quite rightly so that The Good, the Bad and the Ugly is the best of the Dollars trilogy. For me my favourite of this trio hands down is this absolute masterpiece of cinema. Lee Van Cleef, Clint Eastwood, and Gian Maria Volonté exude extreme cool from the opening scenes to the climatic end duel, all of them bringing commanding performances. So many iconic shots, sequences, and lines of dialogue have fully imprinted themselves into my mind. Sergio Leoni was truly the master adapting Japanese cinema and here it's no less obvious in it brilliance and simplicity. The old school sound effects and Ennio Morricones iconic score permeating throughout is such a joy to the ears. I will never grow tired of watching this film, to me this is the iconic Western upon which all others must stand against.

Wow. I already thought the first one was great, but this is one hell of a step up. Genuinely a complete movie and one of the best westerns I've ever seen. The main reason being: it finally gets a notable side character, a memorable villain, and more complex / variable intentions among all parties. And the 'notable side character' arguably has just as much, if not more screen presence than Clint eastwood, which I never would've expected. Van cleef is fucking incredible in this movie and I couldn't believe someone could be more imposing than clint, in what is pretty much his film. Insane addition to the movie and changes everything about it. The contrast in their personalities and different approaches to the same problem that their characters make is so nice to watch, their dynamic is at its best with the hat shootout. And then you have indio and his gang, a memorable villain with a more nuanced backstory and intentions that always keep changing. It's a much better, more refined story that is less predictable yet easier to follow, and that's exactly what the first one was missing. The intro credits as usual are innovative and so cool. The cinematography is incredible, beautiful landscapes, stunning shot framing, insanely operatic showdowns and innovative camerawork. And the night sequences are especially stunning, I really mean it. Then you have the shootouts. It takes the showdowns of fistful of dollars to another level - longer, higher stakes, less predictable, and the score behind all of it elevates it to another level. One of the best western scores ever, and it is so essential to the movie here, it's incredible. I love how every character has his own sound motif, and the cherry ontop is the music box motif used so perfectly in the finale. The final showdown was just insane. As a whole, it's a complete movie that I can't fault in any way. It's decisively better than 'For a fistful of dollars', as good as it was. And after seeing 'The good, the bad and the ugly', I can confidently say that this one is the best of the 3. It's just got the formula totally nailed down, I see it as the perfect balance between the first and third movies - introducing the all-important van cleef, having a more nuanced story & memorable villain, yet retaining a more concise runtime, and not having to split the screentime across 3 main leads (I didn't like Wallach in TGTBTU that much). It's an amazing movie.

I personally enjoyed this movie more than A Fistful of Dollars (although the first one is still amazing). Eastwood was as iconic as usual, but the amazing acting of Lee Van Cleef as Douglas Mortimer was something I was not expecting to see. Just one movie left to finish this amazing trilogy.

For a Few Dollars More de Sergio Leone est un chef d’œuvre. Ce western met en scène deux chasseurs de prime amenés à se rencontrer et à partager la même mission. Ainsi, Manco et le colonel Mortimer mettrons en place plusieurs stratagèmes pour mettre la main sur El Indio, venant de s’évader de prison, ainsi que sa bande. Cette seconde réalisation pour la trilogie du Dollars est à mon sens la meilleure. On nous donne deux acteurs d’exemptions ( Clint Eastwood et Lee Van Cleef ) amenés a travailler ensemble contre El Indio ( joué par Gian María Volonté ). L’intrigue est très bonne et met en place un scénario super bien fondé. Ici, il sera beaucoup plus question de justice mais avec quelques contraste, Manco fait justice et s’enrichit tandis que Mortimer est à la recherche d’une réel justice. La Vengeance est ici le thème principal du film et il sera amenés au fur et à mesure avec des flashbacks. La mélodie de la montre est aussi un son iconique du film ainsi qu’un élément centrale du film. Beaucoup de scènes sont iconique et représentent énormément de chose, comme la scènes des chapeau qui n’est pas une scène de duels mais plutôt de démonstration pour savoir qui est le meilleur. Le film nous montre que la vengeance peut rapidement devenir une prison, Mortimer se venge mais le passé ne change pas, il n’obtiendra donc qu’une victoire amère.
